correctness.rationale: The total-population equation gives the exact full-system eigenvalue \(-\mu\). Eliminating the total-population direction yields the displayed five-dimensional tangent Jacobian. An independent exact-rational replay of the inspected verifier reproduced the affine polynomial \(\det(J_{\mathrm{tan}}+\mu I)\) and its unique root \(\mathcal R_\times=386467087274709075099662209/386355335676178838352248250=1.0002892456456818\ldots\). For \(1<\mathcal R_0<\mathcal R_\times\), positivity of this nonzero determinant in odd real dimension contradicts all shifted eigenvalues lying in the closed left half-plane, so some tangent eigenvalue has real part greater than \(-\mu\). At the root, \(-\mu\) is a tangent eigenvalue. The argument does not claim stability on the whole interval or dominance above the crossing.
